remarks_1999: Not recorded Whitney Archive, Downtown Gallery Archive, Abiquiú Notebooks. On verso is burnished image of another cityscape. O'Keeffe wrote: "This is what I saw out a window where I lived for a short time" (*Some Memories of Drawings* [1988], unpaginated, text accompanying entry 14). Between 1925 and 1932 O'Keeffe and Stieglitz lived winters at the Shelton Hotel, taking rooms there as available on various floors. In *Some Memories of Drawings* O'Keeffe may be referring to the period in 1926 when they lived in rooms on the 11th floor that provided a view to the west of St. Patrick's Cathedral (the 24 April 1926 issue of *The Sheldon Spotlight*, published weekly by the hotel with news about its guests, confirms her living in rooms on the 11th floor). But later that year and again in 1927, when Frances O'Brien interviewed her for an article published in *The Nation* (12 October 1927), O'Keeffe was living on the 28th floor. By early 1928, when she was interviewed for an article in *Time* (20 February 1928), she was living on the 30th floor. A setback on the 16th floor allowed for "a large sun parlor, a charming roof garden and a dining room with a roof terrace" ("A Giant Hotel For None But Men," *New York Hotel Record* [19 September 1923], 30). The setback also provided unobstructed views of New York from all directions and, because of that, this drawing could have been made any time between 1925 and 1932, using a view from these public spaces of the 16th floor of the hotel. But, typically, O'Keeffe's views of the city from an elevated point are those she had from windows in apartments she occupied, and thus this drawing is dated 1926 when, in the early part of the year, her apartment had a view west from the 11th floor. (Source: Lynes, 1999)
remarks_post_1999: Lynes publication dates this work as 1926. Fine Arts Museums of San Francisco changed date to 1924–1926 in 2023. (Source: Information provided for *Access O'Keeffe* by Fine Arts Museums of San Francisco, 2025)

credit_line: Fine Arts Museums of San Francisco, Gift of Mrs. Charlotte S. Mack, 1961.48.1
description: A hazy, abstracted view of the New York City skyline. In the foreground is a wide, multistory building rendered without detail in a single shade of gray. Behind this building, two black spires rise from the top of a cathedral-like structure. Other structures fade into the background, visible only as faint geometric shapes.
